SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.status AS tenant_status,
  r.name AS role_name,
  u.email AS user_email,
  u.status AS user_status,
  CASE WHEN u.last_login_at IS NULL THEN 'never' ELSE CAST(u.last_login_at AS varchar) END AS last_login,
  CASE WHEN u.last_login_at IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(u.last_login_at AS date)) END AS days_since_last_login,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(u.created_at AS date)) AS account_age_days,
  COUNT(*) OVER() AS total_qualifying_rows
FROM user_roles ur
JOIN roles r ON r.id = ur.role_id
JOIN users u ON u.id = ur.user_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = u.tenant_id
WHERE r.name IN ('Owner','Administrator')
  AND u.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND u.status = 'active'
  AND (u.last_login_at IS NULL OR u.last_login_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-05')
ORDER BY u.last_login_at ASC NULLS FIRST, t.name ASC, u.email ASC, r.name ASC
LIMIT 50

  AND u.deleted_at IS NULL

ORDER BY u.last_login_at ASC NULLS FIRST, t.name ASC, u.email ASC, r.name ASC
LIMIT 50
note: Grain is one row per (user, role) since a user can hold both Owner and Administrator and role_name is a report column; days_since_last_login is left NULL for 'never' rather than a sentinel number, with never-logged-in users sorted first via last_login_at ASC NULLS FIRST (most stale). total_qualifying_rows is a window-count column showing how many rows matched in total, since more than 50 may qualify.

Submitted. Summary of what the report delivers:

- **Grain:** one row per (user, role) — Owner/Administrator, active, dormant (never logged in or last login before 2025-10-05), excluding soft-deleted users.
- **Columns:** tenant name/status, role name, user email/status, last login (or 'never'), days since last login, account age in days, plus a total-matching-rows count.
- **Ordering:** never-logged-in users first, then oldest last-login dates first (most stale first), tie-broken by tenant name, email, role.
- **Cap:** 50 rows printed; `total_qualifying_rows` shows the full count if more qualify.
